sections.h2: Where is Grady County and which towns sit inside it?
sections.html:
Grady County lies along Georgia's southern border with Florida. Cairo is the seat and the most populous city. The county dates from August 17, 1905, when the General Assembly cut it from parts of Decatur and Thomas; its namesake is Henry W. Grady, an orator and editor of the Atlanta Constitution (Wikipedia).

The county spans 460 square miles, 455 of them land. Water here mostly flows into the Ochlockonee River, with the northwest corner draining toward the Flint, and the Red Hills Region extends into the county. Its neighbors are Mitchell to the north, Thomas to the east and Decatur to the west, with the Florida counties of Leon and Gadsden along the south.

Cairo and Whigham are the only incorporated cities. Calvary is a census-designated place, and Beachton and Spence are unincorporated communities. Grady County Schools operates six public schools, including Cairo High School. All real property lands on a single county digest, though a city may levy its own tax as well, so read each line of the bill before you settle on a price.

sections.h2: What do the Census figures say about Grady County?
sections.html:
Growth has been gradual. Wikipedia's census table shows 18,457 people in 1910, 18,015 in 1960, 23,659 in 2000 and 25,011 in 2010. The county had 26,236 residents at the 2020 census, and the July 2025 estimate of 26,590 is a 1.4% increase. About one in five people (21.2%) is 65 or older, so age-based exemptions matter to many owners planning a move.

sections.h2: Which Grady County offices handle valuation and billing?
sections.html:
Billing and valuation are split between two offices. The commissioner bills real property, personal property, vehicles, mobile homes and timber. Returns, valuation and applications for conservation or agricultural assessment go to the Tax Assessor office, headed by a chief appraiser.

  • Tax commissioner, per the qPublic site: 114 1st Street NE, Cairo, GA 39828, property phone 229-377-3322, open Monday to Thursday from half past seven in the morning until six in the evening, shut on Fridays.
  • County service pages for the commissioner and the assessor: 33 17th Avenue NW, Cairo, GA 39827, with eight-to-five weekday hours.
  • Parcel lookup: the commissioner's qPublic site has a search tool covering each parcel.

The two pages differ on address and hours, so phone 229-377-3322 before going in person and ask which counter takes your payment. Updates appear on the county's commissioner page and assessor page.

sections.h2: How does a Grady County assessment appeal work?
sections.html:
Georgia taxes 40% of a property's January 1 fair market value, and the assessors send a yearly notice with both figures. Disagreement goes in a letter to the Board of Tax Assessors, postmarked inside 45 days of the notice's mailing date. The letter picks a path (Board of Equalization, hearing officer or arbitrator) on state form PT-311A (Georgia Department of Revenue FAQ).

The 2024 cycle in Grady ran late. A delayed revaluation pushed assessment notices into September, and the county told owners that some appeal windows would end October 28 and others October 31. It added that the digest would reach the tax commissioner behind schedule, that the rate could not be set until December, and that commissioners expected a significant decrease in the mill rate after the revaluation (county notice).

Keep the notice and any appeal letter with your closing papers, because a title company working out a payoff may ask which value the bill rests on.

sections.h2: What due date will a Grady County bill show?
sections.html:
The state's default deadline is December 20. The Department of Revenue's Grady facts page adds that local officials may choose December 1 or November 15 instead, or bill in installments, so the printed date on your bill governs. Interest waits until 60 days after the bill's postmark, and penalties may follow on what stays unpaid (Grady County property tax facts).

For an overdue parcel, get penalty and interest figures from the commissioner. Three other fixed points apply here:

  • Returns for property held on January 1 are taken from January 1 through April 1.
  • A mobile home located in the county on January 1 is returned for tax by April 1, together with the location permit.
  • A claim for refund of wrongly assessed tax has to start within three years of payment.

sections.h2: Which exemptions and special assessments can Grady County owners claim?
sections.html:
You may file for homestead at any point after moving in, and April 1 is the last day for the first year. The assessor's page cites code section 48-5-44, and the state treats a missed filing as a waiver. The state's standard deduction takes $2,000 off assessed value. The Department's Grady facts page lists no local amounts on top of that, though it is dated 2016, so ask the assessor whether newer ones exist.

A county notice from January 2025 said the commissioners intended to opt out of the statewide adjusted base year homestead exemption and scheduled hearings for February 17 and 18, 2025. Ask the assessor how that affects your home before you tell a buyer the value is frozen.

  • Conservation use or preferential agricultural assessment: file between January 1 and April 1.
  • Freeport exemption on commercial and industrial inventory: available only where local voters adopted it, with filing on the return schedule.
  • A buyer files separately, since an exemption does not pass with the deed.

sections.h2: What did the county's 2026 millage notice say?
sections.html:
A county notice dated November 2026 said the Board of Commissioners had tentatively adopted a millage rate that raises property taxes by 4.72 percent. It printed a tentative rate of 12.64 mills, up .57 mill, compared with 12.070 mills at most without the increase, and listed three hearings that month at 33 17th Avenue NW in Cairo (county notice).

The figure speaks only to the county's own levy. School and city rates come separately, and final numbers show on the bill. For a payoff figure, request the adopted rates from the commissioner's office.

sections.h2: How should a Grady County seller handle tax at closing?
sections.html:
Who owns the parcel on January 1 carries that year's liability. Under the Department of Revenue's reading, a sale on January 2 still leaves the January 1 owner responsible, and nothing is refunded for part of a year. The contract and the settlement statement therefore divide the bill and should show who pays what.

  • Ask the commissioner what is owed on the parcel for this year and any earlier year.
  • Tell the closing agent about any open appeal so a revised bill can be handled.
  • Give the closing agent the payoff figure and the office that takes the payment.
  • Tell the office once a homestead exemption stops applying because you have left.

Even a buyer paying cash for the house as-is takes the parcel with its tax history, so any arrears belong on the settlement statement.

faqs.q: Where can I pay Grady County property tax in person?
faqs.a: Go to the tax commissioner's office in Cairo. The commissioner's own page gives 114 1st Street NE with Monday to Thursday hours, while the county service page gives 33 17th Avenue NW with weekday hours of eight to five. Call 229-377-3322 first to learn which counter takes payment.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to contest a Grady County value?
faqs.a: You get 45 days counted from the mailing date. Your letter must carry a postmark within that period, go to the Board of Tax Assessors on state form PT-311A, and name your route.

faqs.q: Does Grady County offer its own homestead exemptions?
faqs.a: The state's county facts page, dated 2016, shows only the statewide ones. Because of the county's 2025 opt-out notice, ask the assessor which freeze rules cover your home now.

faqs.q: If I close a Grady County sale in March, who owes that year's tax?
faqs.a: The January 1 owner is liable. With no partial-year refund available, the contract and settlement statement set the split, and the commissioner can confirm the amount before you close.

faqs.q: Is a refund possible for Grady County tax paid in error?
faqs.a: Yes, when the tax was erroneously or illegally assessed and collected. Make a written request within three years of paying. For an appealed assessment, the refund is handled automatically after the final taxable value is set.
